y: Used as a pronoun to replace an adverbial phrase starting with à.
With verbs: see Appendix:French verbs followed by à for verbs which use this structure.
在这儿，那儿；去这儿，去那儿
y a pas le feu au lac: alternative form of il n'y a pas le feu au lac
y a-t-il: subject-inverted form of il y a; is there? are there?, (after a modal adverb) there is, there are
y aller: to go about something, to proceed in a certain manner

y avoir anguille sous roche: for there to be something fishy and suspicious going on, for there to be something in the wind, in the offing
y avoir de l'eau dans le gaz: /i a.vwaʁ də l‿o dɑ̃ l(ə) ɡaz/
for there to be trouble brewing, for there to be trouble in paradise, for there to be tension in the air
y avoir fort à parier: for it to be very probable that
y avoir mille à parier: for it to be very probable that
y avoir péril en la demeure: for there to be danger in delay
y avoir un avant et un après: for there to be a before and an after
y compris: including (being part of the group or topic just mentioned)
y en a des qui: Less formal alternative of il y en a des qui
y laisser des plumes: not to come out of it unscathed, to come out of it battered and bruised
y mettre du sien: to do one's bit, to do one's part, to show some goodwill, to demonstrate some willingness
y perdre son latin: alternative form of en perdre son latin
y rester: to kick the bucket, to buy it, to check out (to die)
y'a plus de jeunesse: alternative form of il n'y a plus de jeunesse
